artifacts.title: Myers v. Illiana Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: An elder appealed Presbytery’s elevation, without additional process, of suspensions from office and the Sacraments to deposition and excommunication. The SJC granted the appeal, reversed in whole, and remanded, restoring the prior suspensions. Elevation required a hearing on incorrigibility and contumacy—with a charge, evidence, plea, and defense—but not a full de novo trial; disagreement with the original verdict alone was insufficient. The SJC left unresolved deposition from office when excommunication is absent.

artifacts.synopsis: A minister appealed a judgment finding him guilty on most charges and imposing six months’ suspension. The SJC held BCO 32-20 barred Specifications 1, 2, and 4 because Presbytery lacked extraordinary justification for prosecuting old allegations, but did not bar ongoing Specification 3. It separately found the entire process constitutionally flawed and prejudicial. The SJC reversed the whole censure, declined Presbytery’s requested harsher sentence, and concluded the matter. A concurrence disputed the majority’s BCO 32-20 interpretation while agreeing with the result.

artifacts.synopsis: After Korean Eastern Presbytery tried, convicted, deposed, and excommunicated TE Eliot Lee, the SJC sustained his appeal and reversed the disposition and excommunication. The decisive reason was procedural: the record did not show timely service of the indictment/citations or the required 14-day trial notice, violating BCO 32-3, 32-7, and 32-10. Under BCO 42-9, the SJC rendered the decision it thought should have been made, finding no strong presumption of guilt under BCO 31-2 justified formal process; it added pastoral counsel, expressly not censure.
